kept.claim: Reminders that can never be sent because sendTo is missing or the message is empty (line 158), or because workflowStep/booking is null (line 68), never get retryCount incremented, so they are still re-queried and skipped every cron run until their date passes — the exact behaviour the PR aims to stop.
kept.evidence:
In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts, retryCount is incremented in only two places: the `else` branch after `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value (lines 178-186) and the `catch` block (lines 189-197). Two earlier exits skip both:
(1) Lines 68-70, `if (!reminder.workflowStep || !reminder.booking) continue;`, which runs before the try block.
(2) Line 158, `if (message?.length && message?.length > 0 && sendTo)`, which has no else branch.

Both inputs can be missing. At lines 75-78, `sendTo` is `reminder.booking?.smsReminderNumber` for any action other than SMS_NUMBER, and that field is nullable. At line 103 `message` starts as `reminderBody || null`, and it stays null when there is no reminderBody and the template is not REMINDER (lines 145-156).

Such a reminder keeps `scheduled: false` and its retryCount never rises. The findMany at lines 48-60 therefore fetches it again on every cron run. The new `retryCount > 1` delete at lines 38-42 never matches it, so it is only removed by the `scheduledDate <= now` branch at lines 32-37. That is the same behaviour as before the PR.

The claim is technically accurate. The cost is extra DB re-fetching and possibly a `prisma.profile.findFirst` call per run, not repeated Twilio calls. That fits the MEDIUM gap severity. The proposed fix (increment on every non-success outcome, or delete directly) is sound and does not change the success path.

kept.claim: The new `retryCount > 1` OR-branch in deleteMany has no `method: SMS` filter, so the SMS cron deletes EMAIL/WHATSAPP reminders with retryCount > 1 and the branch cannot use the (method, scheduled, scheduledDate) index.
kept.evidence: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:29-45 the deleteMany is `where: { OR: [ { method: SMS, scheduledDate: { lte: now } }, { retryCount: { gt: 1 } } ] }`. The second OR branch has no `method` filter, so it matches any WorkflowReminder row with retryCount > 1, whatever its method. packages/prisma/schema.prisma:987-1007 shows that `retryCount` is a generic column (`Int @default(0)`) on the shared WorkflowReminder model. That model holds SMS, EMAIL and WHATSAPP rows, and its only method-prefixed index is `@@index([method, scheduled, scheduledDate])`. There is no index on retryCount, so that branch cannot use an index. A grep for `retryCount` finds writes only in scheduleSMSReminders.ts (lines 184 and 195, which increment it only for rows fetched with `method: SMS` at lines 47-60). So today no non-SMS row can reach retryCount > 1, and the cross-method deletion is latent. The draft says this outright ("Works today only because no other code sets retryCount"), so it is not presenting a hypothetical as a current bug. The OR clause is still missing the SMS scope, and the index point is correct. The suggested fix (move `method: SMS` to the top level and keep both conditions in the OR) keeps the intended behaviour and scopes the delete correctly.

kept.claim: Transient failures (Twilio 5xx/network errors, a temporary SMS lock where scheduleSMS returns undefined) are counted the same as permanent ones, so a ~30 minute outage (two 15-min cron runs) permanently deletes every pending SMS reminder in the 7-day window.
kept.evidence:
The claim holds when checked against the code.

- **Every failure counts the same.** In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts, lines 178-187 add 1 to `retryCount` whenever `scheduleSMS` returns a falsy value. Lines 189-197 add 1 on any exception, with no check of the error type. So a Twilio 5xx, a network timeout, a `checkSMSRateLimit` throw or a missing-credentials error counts exactly like a permanent 4xx such as an invalid number.
- **Deletion comes quickly.** At the start of each run, lines 29-45 delete every row with `retryCount > 1`. The count goes 0 -> 1 on run N and 1 -> 2 on run N+1, and the row is deleted at the start of run N+2.
- **Runs are 15 minutes apart.** .github/workflows/cron-scheduleSMSReminders.yml:8 sets `*/15 * * * *`, so two failed runs about 15 minutes apart are enough for a reminder to be deleted permanently.
- **The failure hits a whole week of reminders at once.** The query at lines 48-60 fetches every unscheduled SMS reminder due within the next 7 days. One bad window therefore affects all of them.
- **The lock case counts as a failure too.** In packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/providers/twilioProvider.ts, `scheduleSMS` returns `undefined` when `isLockedForSMSSending` is true, which lands in the `else` branch at line 178 and increments the count.
- **Before the PR, failures healed themselves.** The base version only logged the error, so the row stayed `scheduled: false` and the next run retried it.

Two points are slightly overstated but do not change the verdict:
- Deleting reminders for a locked team may be acceptable or even intended, since the lock exists to stop abuse. The transient-error case is the main issue.
- The 30-minute window assumes the outage covers two consecutive cron runs.

The suggested fix (count only 4xx errors other than 429, and treat the lock case separately) is reasonable and would not break anything else.

kept.claim: The prisma.update inside the catch block is unguarded; if it throws (e.g. P2025 because the reminder was deleted by a concurrent booking cancellation), the error escapes the for-loop and aborts processing of all remaining reminders in that run.
kept.evidence: In packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts, the `catch (error)` block at about lines 189-197 now starts with `await prisma.workflowReminder.update({ where: { id: reminder.id }, data: { retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 } })`, and nothing wraps that call in its own try/catch. Before this PR (per the diff against 917c7b07), the catch block only called console.log, so a failed reminder could never stop the loop. Prisma's `update` throws P2025 (record not found) when the `where` clause matches no row. The loop at line 71 handles reminders one at a time and awaits both `twilio.scheduleSMS` and the prisma updates, so a run can take long enough for a booking cancellation to delete a WorkflowReminder row in the meantime. There is a direct path to this failure: if the row was deleted, the `update` inside the try block (scheduled: true, or the retry bump in the new else branch) throws P2025 first. Control then moves to the catch block, whose `update` hits the same missing row and throws again. That exception escapes the for loop, `res.status(200)` is never reached, defaultHandler returns an error, and every reminder after it goes unprocessed until the next cron run. A transient DB error would have the same effect. The side point also holds: `reminder.retryCount + 1` is a read-modify-write based on the earlier findMany, not an atomic `{ increment: 1 }`. The suggested fix (updateMany with increment, with its own .catch) keeps the intended behaviour and prevents the abort. LOW severity is appropriate.
